## Understanding the problem

Given an array `nums` of length n, produce an array of length n−1 where `answer[i] = nums[i] | nums[i+1]`. Example: `[1,3,7,15]` → `[1|3, 3|7, 7|15] = [3,7,15]`. Constraints are tiny (n ≤ 100), so a single linear pass is all that is required — there is no algorithmic subtlety, only implementing the bitwise OR correctly.
k: OR of two numbers sets every bit set in either operand — a single `|` operator per pair suffices.
The output length is exactly n−1; iterating i from 0 to n−2 covers all adjacent pairs exactly once.

a.i: Just compute the OR of each consecutive pair. Nothing smarter is needed or possible — every output element depends on exactly two inputs.
s: Allocate an answer array of size n−1.
For each i in [0, n−2], set answer[i] = nums[i] | nums[i+1].
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the array.
a.sp: O(1) extra space besides the required output.

## Wrap-up

This is a warm-up bit-manipulation problem. The only mistakes possible are off-by-one errors on the output length or confusing `|` with `||`/`^`. A natural follow-up is the same task with AND or XOR, which changes nothing structurally.
